title: What If Your Helmet Filled With Water in Space? One Did

scenes.text: What if your spacesuit helmet filled with water in space? It happened to a real astronaut.
In July 2013, Luca Parmitano was about ninety minutes into a spacewalk when he felt water behind his head.
In zero gravity, water doesn't sink to the bottom. It gathers in a blob and clings to you.
Surface tension pulled it forward, over his ears, his eyes, and then his nose. He couldn't hear his partner.
Roughly one to one and a half liters leaked in. A NASA board later called it life-threatening.
It took about twenty minutes to get him back inside. He very well could have drowned, in space.
